why: The question asks for a Q4 2027 year-over-year quarterly change, not a full-year figure, so the code-set day 2028-03-30 (90 days after the calendar year-end, basis expected_publication) does not apply to it.

The figure is a survey's rolling twelve-month share (2026-07-07 to 2027-07-07), not a year's figure, and neither the thesis nor the article gives its publication day, so the due day 2027-07-07 is just the window's end and its basis expected_publication is untrue.

The article says 'NVIDIA said it will file its fiscal 2027 annual report on Form 10-K on February 24, 2027', so the due day should be 2027-02-24 with basis stated, not the code day 2027-04-01 with basis expected_publication.
The question asks for a rolling twelve-month share running from 2026-07-07 to about mid-2027, not a year's figure, so the code-set day 2027-03-31 for year 2026 falls before the figure's period ends.

The thesis checks Ornn's published spot index 'at year-end 2026' and the question asks for the price on December 31, 2026, which is one day's price and not a year's figure, so the code day 2027-03-31 with basis expected_publication contradicts the check date the thesis gives.
